newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open little changed Monday as dealers expected trading to be subdued with LIFFE shut due to a bank holiday.
"With London closed, I don't think much is going to happen today," a trader said. "It's going to be relatively quiet."

Friday, New York cocoa futures posted losses for the sixth straight session, sagging to two-months lows, on continued speculative liquidation. July ended down $12 at $1,379 a tonne near the bottom of today's $1,392 to $1,376 range. Spot May ended $12 lower at $1,368, while the back months sagged $5 to $10.
Technically, July support was seen at $1,365-1,360, while resistance was pegged near Friday's high ot $1,392. Major resistance awaited at $1,400, followed by $1,418.
The London market will reopen Tuesday. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
